purpose: Align historical static and browser contracts with the canonical Surface Standard runtime, and escalate any falsified runtime assumption into the effective standard rather than masking it in evidence consumers.

saturationImpact.reason: Historical alignment exposed one stable post-decision runtime vocabulary regression; later Enterprise 1.8 browser failures are stale evidence consumers and do not add runtime primitives.

invariants.name: semantic-token-declaration
invariants.rule: Historical design-system assurance validates the declared CSS custom-property syntax --ds-ease:, not the invalid literal --ds-ease;.

invariants.name: progressive-settings-sequencing
invariants.rule: Browser journeys fill organization fields while the organization disclosure is open, then open provider and fill provider fields.

invariants.name: progressive-job-sequencing
invariants.rule: Browser journeys open criteria and schedule job groups before interacting with controls moved into those groups.

invariants.name: canonical-terminal-vocabulary
invariants.rule: Historical browser assertions consume Accetta nel catalogo, Accettata nel catalogo and Scarica evidenza.

invariants.name: no-runtime-bypass
invariants.rule: Alignment does not force hidden controls, disable single-open behavior, modify server authority, or reintroduce legacy labels in production code.

invariants.name: same-head-evidence
invariants.rule: Historical-contract assurance, Surface Standard assurance, server-backed browser and general CI execute against the same PR head before maturity.

invariants.name: stable-post-toggle-observation
invariants.rule: Single-open browser assertions observe stable state after details toggle reconciliation using bounded condition waiting, not instantaneous counts or arbitrary sleeps.

invariants.name: direct-rerender-terminal-reconciliation
invariants.rule: A human source decision that directly reconstructs source dialog emits ictc:surface-changed after reconstruction so terminal layers reconcile stable DOM.

invariants.name: legacy-visual-journey-terminal-shell
invariants.rule: The retained Enterprise 1.8 visual regression journey executes against the candidate runtime and therefore asserts current terminal shell vocabulary and progressive disclosure while preserving its geometry, role, keyboard and overflow budgets.

observedFailures.observation: browser-product-check opened provider after organization and then attempted to fill organizationName after single-open behavior hid that section.
The revised journey asserted instantaneous open-section count while details toggle reconciliation was closing the previous sibling.
The canonical decision completed, but renderSourceDialog rebuilt base Verificata/Stato umano after refresh-time terminal pass.

The retained 1.8 visual journey still asserted the pre-candidate document title and navigation vocabulary while running against the current 2.0 terminal candidate, and repeated old settings disclosure ordering.

preventiveAlignments.reason: authorities and sourceHints are owned by closed criteria/schedule groups and must be opened before interaction.
historical journeys consume canonical terminal vocabulary so stable regressions back to legacy copy remain observable.
older-version visual journeys preserve geometry, accessibility, role and interaction invariants while consuming the current candidate shell when they are executed inside that candidate.

acceptance: The semantic-token historical check passes without changing the design-system CSS token declaration.
Product and retained Enterprise 1.8 browser journeys complete settings through single-open progressive disclosure.
The product journey completes job configuration by opening each required disclosure owner.
Single-open assertions use Playwright condition assertions rather than arbitrary sleeps.
After a human source decision, direct source-dialog rerender emits ictc:surface-changed and stable post-decision copy remains canonical.

The retained Enterprise 1.8 journey asserts current terminal title/navigation/content vocabulary while keeping its original home-height, recommendation-height, event-queue, role, keyboard, overflow and minimum-target budgets.
No API permission, capability or backend authority is weakened by this slice.
Surface Standard assurance, server-backed UI-standard browser, all historical browser journeys, contract audit, runtime E2E and security are re-evaluated on the same final PR head.
claimBoundary: This model demonstrates historical-contract alignment and runtime corrections falsified by that alignment. It does not establish universal regression freedom, accessibility conformance, legal compliance, certification or production readiness.
